rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘not subject to judgment’ means not subdued, owned, tested, or held to account in the trial of this world.
rows.anchor: أي مقهورين مملوكين مجربين محاسبين بما عملتم في دار البلاء

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī derives dāna from humility and submission.
rows.anchor: وأصل تركيب ( دان ) للذل والانقياد - قاله البيضاوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Return it’ means return the soul to its former state.
rows.anchor: ترجعونها } أي الروح إلى ما كانت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge to restore the soul at the throat proves their inability and binds them to acknowledge resurrection: if God does not decree death, why can they not avert it?
rows.anchor: وهذا دليل على أنه لا حياة لمن بلغت روحه الحلقوم أصلا وهذا إلزام لهم بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If death is decreed and cannot be treated, resurrection is likewise decreed and unavoidable; denying one while accepting the other is obstinacy.
rows.anchor: لزمكم الإقرار بأن البعث مقدر لا يمكن علاجه , فإن أنكرتم أحدهما فأنكروا الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if they claim not to know death is decreed, their inability to resist it despite their aversion and status shows its decree.
rows.anchor: لو لم يكن بتقديره لأمكنت مقاومته وقتا ما لا سيما والنفوس مجبولة على كراهته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denials of messengers, the miraculous Book, and rain’s divine source show a rejection of God’s acts that would leave the world purposeless.
rows.anchor: إن أرسل إليكم رسولا قلتم : ساحر كذاب , وإن صدقه مرسله بكتاب معجز قلتم : سحر وافتراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The summons of a worldly king is for accounting; by analogy, God sends messengers to summon people for reckoning.
rows.anchor: فكما أن ملوك الدنيا لا يرسل أحد منهم إلى أحد من رعيته فيأخذه قهرا إلا للدينونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s sending is not to learn the dead person’s state or ease it, since God already knows and only permits what He commands through His messengers.
rows.anchor: ولا ليعلم حاله بوجه من الوجوه بل الأمر كما قيل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unattributed verse says that once a person is hidden, thought cannot reveal useful information about him.
rows.anchor: إذا غيب المرء استسر حديثه ولم يخبر الأفكار عنه بما يغني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since they admit God created them from dust and returns them to dust, they must admit He can raise them from dust for judgment.
rows.anchor: يلزمكم حتما أن تقروا بأنه قادر على أن يعيدكم من التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God divides the resurrected into three groups so each receives what it deserves.
rows.anchor: لنجازي كلا بما يستحق ونقسمهم إلى أزواج ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foremost are those whom God draws from themselves near to Him; they are chosen before they themselves seek.
rows.anchor: أي السابقين الذين اجتذبهم الحق من أنفسهم فقربهم منه فكانوا مرادين قبل أن يكونوا مريدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their nearness is not spatial, since God is transcendent, but comes through acquiring noble qualities within human capacity.
rows.anchor: وليس القرب قرب مكان لأنه تعالى منزهه عنه , وإنما هو بالتخلق بالصفات الشريفة على قدر الطاقة البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foremost have shed desires and independent will, acting only as commanded; the will belongs to God.
rows.anchor: لا شهوات لهم فلا أغراض فلا فعل إلا أمروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s purpose is to affirm the universal message through resurrection to the three groups described in the preceding surahs, since God possesses every perfection and is free of defect.
rows.anchor: عموم الرسالة لعموم الإلهية بالبعث إلى الأزواج الثلاثة المذكورة في السورتين الماضيتين من الثقلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of resurrection entails struggle against those who disobey the Messenger, including fighting and spending, to turn them from bodily deficiencies toward spiritual qualities.
rows.anchor: المقتضي لجهاد من يحتاج إلى الجهاد ممن عصى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالسيف وما ترتب عليه من النفقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s universal mission, caliphate, widespread call, and large community demonstrate his superiority over earlier messengers to the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: فضيلة هذا الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم على جمكيع من تقدمه من الرسل عليهم الصلاة والسلام بعموم رسالته وشمول خلافته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the numbered arrangement, this surah closes the first half and the next opens the second, completing the purpose of the surah that began the sequence.
rows.anchor: لتكون هذه السورة التي هي آخر النصف الأول والتي بعدها التي هي أول النصف الثاني من حيث العدد غاية للمقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Isrāʾ and al-Kahf disclose the opening surah’s call to guidance and its warning.
rows.anchor: وهي الإسراء ، وكذا السورة التي هي أول النصف الثاني وهي الكهف كاشفتين لمقصد الأولى فيما دعت إليه من الهداية

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Jābir reports that the Prophet prohibited cupping on Tuesday because al-Ḥadīd was revealed that day; the author gives no grading.
rows.anchor: عن جابر رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala calls God the one whose divinity encompasses all beings.
rows.anchor: الذي أحاطت إلالهيته بجميع الموجودات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes the All-Merciful as extending generosity through every movement and stillness.
rows.anchor: الذي وسعهم جوده فيي جميع الحركات والسكنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes the Especially Merciful as choosing those who please Him through worship.
rows.anchor: الذي خص من بينهم بما له من الاختيار يفي كمال الاقتدار أهل ولا يته بما يرضيه من العبادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage raises God’s allies from faith in the unseen and sensory parables to contemplation of the divine attributes, preparing them to dissolve into the divine presence and fear Him.
rows.anchor: رقاهم إلى التكفر في تفصيل ما اففتح به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun ‘He’ denotes self-existent being, eternally free of nonexistence; none but God deserves it, present to every inward thought yet unseen by the senses through His majesty.
rows.anchor: فلا عدم له أصلا بوجه من الوجوه , فلا يستحق الوصف ب ( هو ) غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is the deity alone worthy of worship, hidden from intellect in His majesty yet manifest through incomparable acts; no creature shares His divinity.
rows.anchor: أي المعبود الذي لا ينبغي العبادة إلا له , الذي بطن بما لم تحط ولا تحيط به العقول

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī describes the name Allah as the locus of hearts and intellects that they cannot apprehend.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي في شرح الأسماء : وهو لوه القلوب والعقول أي محارها الذي لا تدركه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawḥīd of the name al-Ilāh is obligatory and foundational to every duty; affirming the other names is foundational to voluntary acts, and joining both completes religion.
rows.anchor: وهو أساس كل فريضة , وتوحيد سائر الأسماء نقل وهو أساس كل نافلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verbal affirmation protects from bodily punishment in this life, while knowing tawḥīd frees the soul from panic at harm and miserliness when blessed.
rows.anchor: وإن كان علما تخلص من نار الهلع على النفوس في الدنيا , وهو الجزع عند مس الشر

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines al-Ilāh as worshipful submission: one who imagines another can meet a need humbles himself to it.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : والإله : التعبد وهو التذلل , فمن توهم حاجته بشيء وتوهم أن عنده قوام حاجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s being the Knower of the unseen covers what is hidden from every creature; ‘the witnessed’ clarifies that this includes all that some creatures can sense.
rows.anchor: دل بذكر الضد على أن المراد كل ما غاب وكل ما شهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥmān denotes mercy encompassing all, while al-Raḥīm denotes a special mercy for those whom God favors.
rows.anchor: أي العام الرحمة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines mercy as ordering creatures in ways suited to their constitution, nature, and inward aims; comprehensive mercy is raḥmāniyya and particular mercy raḥīmiyya.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي رحمه الله تعالى : والرحمة إجراء الخلق على ما يوافق حسبهم ويلائم خلقهم وخلقهم ومقصد أفئدتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥīm grants general outward and particular inward felicity; only God is truly merciful because creatures’ mercy is limited.
rows.anchor: أي ذو الرحمة العامة المسعدة في الظاهر والرحمة الخاصة المسعدة في الباطن

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the mercy of al-Raḥīm is a special favor granted to some among those already covered by al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : الرحمة من الرحيم اختصاص من شملته الرحمانية بمزية ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is truly al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm, as the cited verses portray everlasting, unsevered divine gift and mercy.
rows.anchor: فلذلك لا رحيم بالحقيقة إلا الله تحقيق علم كما أنه لا رحمان إلا الله بادي معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True kingship requires complete control, governance, accounting for every act, knowledge of hidden states, and full retribution; only God has this knowledge and rule.
rows.anchor: فكان لا ملك في الحقيقة إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives some creatures limited rule over others as a trial; those who claim true sovereignty mislead themselves and others, so the declaration of oneness is repeated with al-Malik.
rows.anchor: أولى الخلق من رفعه بعضهم فوق بعض ما أجرى عليهم اسم الملك فتنة لهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet’s warning against the title ‘king of kings’; the Muslim narration says, ‘There is no king but God.’
rows.anchor: حديث أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه الذي رواه الشيخان وأبو داود والترمذي في حديث الذي يسمى ملك الملوك في رواية المسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Malik is the one who needs nothing and whose will is always realized; the phrase also emphasizes God’s unique rule and majesty.
rows.anchor: الملك } فلا ملك في الحقيقة إلا هو لأنه لا يحتاج إلى شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human kingship can lead from honor to luxury, disobedience, arrogance, pride, and disbelief; the source traces Adam’s command from prophethood to caliphate to kingship.
rows.anchor: فإن أمر الله في آدم على ماهو نبوة ثم ينزل فيصير خلافة ثم ينتهي نزوله فيكون ملكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning kingship and its blameworthy consequences, the text names God al-Quddūs: utterly pure from any defect sensed, imagined, anticipated, or inwardly conceived.
rows.anchor: بليغ في النزاهة عن كل وصم يدركه حسن أو يتصوره خيال أو يسبق إليه وهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Holiness is an unchanging purity, and the Prophet chose enduring servitude over the temporary worldly privilege of kingship.
rows.anchor: ولأجل قصر تخلي الخالق بالملك في قليل متاع الدنيا رغب النبي البعد صلى الله عليه وسلم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruling requires patience and knowledge of what sustains worldly order; wisdom is knowing why a ruling is required and what brings a good outcome.
rows.anchor: فالحمل على جميع أنواع الصبر والمصابرة ظاهرا بالإيالة العالية هو الحكم والعلم بالأمر الذي لأجله وجب الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone must learn the rulings relevant to them, while a group should study what applies to all, as commanded in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: وأن ينتدب طائفة لعلم ما يعم جميع الناس

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says wisdom is taught after purification; purification makes one eligible for wisdom, and wisdom eases the burden of legal work.
rows.anchor: فما يعلمهم الحكمة إلا بعد التزكية فمن تزكى فهو من أهلها ومن يترك فليس من أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom makes difficult obligations easy and transforms the soul’s constriction under law into spaciousness; judgment and wisdom depend on broad knowledge.
rows.anchor: فالحكمة تحلي مرارة جهد العمل بالأحكام فييسر بها ما يعسر دونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People possess only the knowledge God grants and receive only a corresponding measure of wisdom, as illustrated by Luqmān.
rows.anchor: ولما لم يكن للخلق من العلم إلا بقدر ما يهبهم الله لم يكن لهم من الحكمة إلا مقدار ما يورثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because all knowledge belongs to God, wisdom and judgment truly belong to Him alone; He is al-Ḥakīm and no one else is truly wise.
rows.anchor: فهو الحكيم الذي لا حكيم إلا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names follow without conjunction because no one attribute conveys the whole meaning of Allah; their totality, as revealed and known through His allies, does.
rows.anchor: أتبعه تلك الأوصاف العلى من غير عطف إعلاما بأنه لا شيء منها يؤدي جميع معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names are not apparent opposites requiring conjunction; each name explains the hidden implication of the preceding one, and the passage’s opening and ending embrace each other.
rows.anchor: كل اسم منها كما مضى شارح لما خفي من الذي قبله ومبين للازمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited command to treat Satan as an enemy is linked to steadfastness and high governance.
rows.anchor: أن الشيطان لكم عدو فاتخذوه عدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s purpose is to show that those professing faith must disavow those marked by hostility, proving their claim as disbelievers disavow believers and reject the truth.
rows.anchor: مقصودها براءة من أقر بالإيمان ممن اتسم بالعدوان دلالة على صحة مدعاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s name, al-Mumtaḥana, signals this purpose: affinity by marriage is the greatest bond after religion, so severing it most clearly marks estrangement and humiliation through disbelief.
rows.anchor: لأن الصهر أعظم الوصل وأشرفها بعد الدين ، فإذا نفى ومنع دل على أعظم المقاطعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala calls God sufficient for whoever seeks refuge in Him, and says His ally needs no other.
rows.anchor: الكافي من لجأ إليه فمن تولاه أغناه عمن سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes the All-Merciful as giving existence and extending mercy through understanding and intellect.
rows.anchor: الذي عم بنعمة الإيجاد من فلق عن وجوده العدم وبراه وشمل ، برحمته البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Especially Merciful grants success to those whom He loves and approves.
rows.anchor: الذي خص بالتوفيق من أحبه وارتضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s purpose is to show that those professing faith must disavow those marked by hostility, proving their claim as disbelievers disavow believers and reject the truth.
rows.anchor: مقصودها براءة من أقر بالإيمان ممن اتسم بالعدوان دلالة على صحة مدعاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s name, al-Mumtaḥana, signals this purpose: affinity by marriage is the greatest bond after religion, so severing it most clearly marks estrangement and humiliation through disbelief.
rows.anchor: لأن الصهر أعظم الوصل وأشرفها بعد الدين ، فإذا نفى ومنع دل على أعظم المقاطعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala calls God sufficient for whoever seeks refuge in Him, and says His ally needs no other.
rows.anchor: الكافي من لجأ إليه فمن تولاه أغناه عمن سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes the All-Merciful as giving existence and extending mercy through understanding and intellect.
rows.anchor: الذي عم بنعمة الإيجاد من فلق عن وجوده العدم وبراه وشمل ، برحمته البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Especially Merciful grants success to those whom He loves and approves.
rows.anchor: الذي خص بالتوفيق من أحبه وارتضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s forgiveness and mercy display His generosity; had people not sinned, He would bring sinners who seek forgiveness so He could forgive them.
rows.anchor: فلو أن الناس لا يذنبون لجاء بقوم يذنبون فيستغفرون فيغفر لهم لتظهر صفة إكرامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghafūr fully covers sins in their essence and effects, and al-Raḥīm grants further generosity after forgiveness.
rows.anchor: أي بالغ الستر للذنوب عينا وأثرا { رحيم * } أي بالغ الإكرام بعد الغفران فضلا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women’s pledge took place on Ṣafā the day after the conquest, after the men’s pledge; the verse was revealed as the Prophet received the women with ʿUmar conveying his instructions below him.
rows.anchor: فأقبل النساء للبيعة عامة ثاني يوم الفتح على الصفا بعد فراغه صلى الله عليه وسلم من بيعة الرجال فنزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: هند بنت عتبة
rows.claim: When the Prophet prohibited theft, Hind said Abū Sufyān was miserly and asked whether taking small amounts from his property was lawful; Abū Sufyān told her it was hers.
rows.anchor: فقالت : إن إبا سفيان رجل شحيح وإني أصيب من ماله هنات فلا أدري أيحل لي أم لا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet recognized the veiled Hind bint ʿUtba, who asked him to forgive her past conduct.
rows.anchor: فقال : ( وإنك لهند بنت عتبة ) , قالت : نعم

rows.speaker: هند بنت عتبة
rows.claim: When told not to commit adultery, Hind retorted that a free woman would not do so.
rows.anchor: فقال : { ولا يزنين } فقال : أو تزني الحرة

rows.speaker: هند بنت عتبة
rows.claim: On the prohibition against killing children, Hind referred to raising children young and the Muslims killing them as adults; her son Ḥanẓala had died at Badr, and ʿUmar laughed while the Prophet smiled.
rows.anchor: ربيناهم صغارا وقتلتموهم كبارا وأنتم وهم أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The slander mentioned in the pledge means attributing to a husband a child who is not his.
rows.anchor: وذكر البهتان وهو أن تقذف ولدا على زوجها ليس منه

rows.speaker: هند بنت عتبة
rows.claim: Hind condemned slander as ugly and said the Prophet called women only to guidance and noble character.
rows.anchor: والله إن البهتان لقبيح وما تدعونا إلا إلى الرشد ومكارم الأخلاق

rows.speaker: هند بنت عتبة
rows.claim: Hind said the women had not gathered intending to disobey the Prophet in anything good.
rows.anchor: ما جلسنا مجلسنا هذا وفي أنفسنا أن نعصيك في شيء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet did not touch a woman’s hand in pledge; when Asmāʾ bint Yazīd asked to pledge by hand, he said he did not shake women’s hands but would accept their pledge.
rows.anchor: وكانت أسماء بنت يزيد بن السكن في المبايعات فقالت : يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī reports that the Prophet used a bowl of water for the women’s pledge, dipping his hand in it before they dipped theirs.
rows.anchor: وعن الشعبي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا بقدح من ماء فغمس يده فيه ثم غمسن أيديهن فيه

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī reports that the Prophet pledged the women to do what they were able, and they replied that God and His Messenger were more merciful to them than themselves.
rows.anchor: وعنه أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لقنهن في المبايعة ( فيما استطعتن وأطقتن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even where women pose no fighting harm, believers may not ally with them until their faith is known; the examination of emigrant women established believers as the standard.
rows.anchor: فعلم نم لك أن تولي النساء مع أنه لا ضرر فيهن بقتال ونحوه لا يسوغ إلا بعد العلم بإيمانهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the closing forgiveness and mercy could encourage favoritism toward unbelieving spouses or kin, the command to disavow every enemy is repeated, linking the ending back to the opening and the pledge and examination verses.
rows.anchor: كرر سبحانه الأمر بالبراءة من كل عدو , ردا لآخر السورة على أولها تأكيدا للإعراض عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoiding the straight course opposes primordial nature and requires inner struggle; the wording uses the tafaʿʿul form, as the surah’s opening used iftiʿāl.
rows.anchor: عبر بالتفعل كما عبر به أول السورة بالافتعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Do not take them as allies’ means do not struggle to make yourselves allied with them; the warning applies first to capable people and a fortiori to others.
rows.anchor: أي تعالجوا أنفسكم أن تتولوا { قوما } أي ناسا لهم قوة على ما يحاولونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s anger covers everyone characterized by these sins, with Jews included first; the verse explains that no good can be expected from them.
rows.anchor: فهو عام في كل من اتصف بذلك يتناول اليهود تناولا أوليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have definitively despaired of any afterlife good because their sins encompass them or because they deny resurrection; an ally may be counted among them and incur their anger.
rows.anchor: أي تحققوا عدم الرجاء { من الآخرة } أي من أن ينالهم منها خير ما لإحاطة معاصيهم بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the rule that only unbelievers despair of God’s relief as further warning against alliance with them.
rows.anchor: ولا ييأس من روح الله إلا القوم الكافرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead learn their resurrection fate, while buried unbelievers form a narrower class whose despair of afterlife good is certain.
rows.anchor: ولما كان من مات فصار أهلا للدفن كشف له عن أحوال القيامة فعرف أنه ناج أو هالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He offers an alternative reading of min as indicating origin: idolaters despair of meeting the buried dead because they deny any reunion or afterlife, despite clear evidence.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { من } ابتدائية فيكون المعنى : كما يئس عباد الأوثان من لقاء من مات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not treat such people as close friends or relatives; neither they nor their allies will prosper, and alliance at minimum ends at death and shares their lasting punishment and shame.
rows.anchor: فلا تتولوا من هذه صفته فيكون بينكم وبينه ما بين القريب مع قريبه من تولى كل منهم من الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s ending reconnects to its beginning, with the passage between them tying the structure together as a concise, comprehensive miracle.
rows.anchor: وقد علم أن هذا الآخر هو أولها , وهذا الموصل مفصلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Also called al-Ḥawāriyyūn, al-Ṣaff urges complete unity in fighting those whom al-Mumtaḥana told believers to disavow, either bringing them to true religion or erasing them from the earth.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الحث على الاجتهاد التام في الاجتماع على قلب واحد في جهاد من دعت الممتحنة إلى البراءة منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This struggle purifies God from association, protects His sacredness from falsehood, and demonstrates sincerity in disavowal and hostility; al-Ṣaff is a result of al-Tawba.
rows.anchor: تنزيها للملك الأعلى عن الشرك ، وصيانة لجنابه الأقدس عن الإفك ، ودلالة على الصدق في البراءة منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Ṣaff best signals the surah’s purpose when its verse and benefits at the beginning, middle, and end are considered; al-Ḥawāriyyūn also conveys it.
rows.anchor: وأدل عما فيها على هذا المقصد الصف بتأمل آيته ، وتدبر ما له من جليل النفع في أوله وأثنائه وغايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala calls God the supreme King, who has all authority because none is His equal.
rows.anchor: الملك الأعظم الذي له الأمر كله لأنه لا كفوء له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The All-Merciful gives everyone the capacity to express acceptance or rejection of what pleases Him.
rows.anchor: الذي عم بنعمة البيان عما يرضيه ممن شاقه ، فقد شرع لكل أحد أن يرده أو يقبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Especially Merciful completes the favor that guides chosen servants to the Abode of Peace and prepares them for it.
rows.anchor: الذي خص بإتمام الإنعام الموصل إلى دار السلام من شاء من عباده فهيأه لذلك وأهله
